Polio survivors’ experiences of a rehabilitation programme were influenced by their self concept and previous experiences of polio.
the patients’ experience of a polio rehabilitation programme is positive and the strategies that they find helpful are not cited within an evidence base to justify service provision.

polio survivors who attend in-patient multi- disciplinary rehabilitation programmes experience long term positive benefits and that these experiences are influenced by their past experiences of poliovirus infection and self- concept.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the lived experience of polio and the importance of self-management and self-efficacy.
the patient’s experience of rehabilitation and the impact of this on their lives.
the lived experience of polio survivors and how this can be incorporated into a rehabilitation programme to ensure patient empowerment and co- production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lived experiences of polio survivors attending a multi-disciplinary in-patient rehabilitation program are positive.
the lived experience of patients with polio and post polio syndrome must be at the forefront of rehabilitation programmes.
the patient’s expertise and lived experience should be at the centre and the heart of a rehabilitation programme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients’ experiences and perceptions of rehabilitation are important in the development and delivery of rehabilitation programmes.

the lived experience of polio survivors must be at the forefront of rehabilitation interventions and that the principles of co production should be adopted to ensure the best possible outcomes for polio survivors.
polio survivors’ views of rehabilitation programmes should be at the heart of service provision.
The main takeaway from our work is that
polio rehabilitation is a long term process that requires the support of a multi-discipline team and that patients must have a central role in the decision-making process.
polio rehabilitation programmes should be co-produced by patients and clinicians.
the patient experience and patient preferences should be at the heart of rehabilitation.
